_help: Short learning card shown after each pin answer. c = course / origin→insertion (+ nerve), f = function, k = clinical correlation. Keys are the Latin answers in pins.json.

ansa cervicalis.c: Loop from C1–C3: superior root rides on the hypoglossal nerve, inferior root from C2–C3; lies on the carotid sheath.
ansa cervicalis.f: Motor to the infrahyoid (strap) muscles – except thyrohyoid (C1 via XII).
ansa cervicalis.k: In thyroid surgery the straps are cut high, where the ansa enters from below, to keep them innervated.

aorta thoracica.c: Continues the arch at T4, runs down left of the vertebral bodies in the posterior mediastinum, leaves at T12 through the aortic hiatus.
aorta thoracica.f: Gives posterior intercostal, bronchial and oesophageal arteries.
aorta thoracica.k: Site of type B aortic dissection – tearing back pain between the shoulder blades.

arcus aortae.c: Arches over the left main bronchus at T4; branches: brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid, left subclavian.
arcus aortae.f: Distributes blood to head and upper limbs.
arcus aortae.k: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under it – an arch aneurysm causes hoarseness.

arteria axillaris.c: From the 1st rib to the lower border of teres major; divided into 3 parts by pectoralis minor.
arteria axillaris.f: Supplies shoulder, axilla and lateral chest wall; becomes the brachial artery.
arteria axillaris.k: Rich collateral network around the scapula allows ligation between thyrocervical trunk and subscapular artery.

arteria carotis communis.c: Right from the brachiocephalic trunk, left from the arch; runs up in the carotid sheath and divides at C4 (upper thyroid cartilage).
arteria carotis communis.f: Supplies head and neck via internal and external carotid.
arteria carotis communis.k: Carotid pulse is felt at the anterior border of SCM; the bifurcation is the classic site of atherosclerotic plaques (stroke).

arteria carotis externa.c: From the bifurcation at C4, ascends into the parotid and ends behind the mandibular neck as maxillary + superficial temporal artery.
arteria carotis externa.f: Supplies face, scalp, neck, thyroid, tongue (8 branches – 'Some Anatomists Like Freaking Out Poor Medical Students').
arteria carotis externa.k: Branches anastomose freely, so it can be ligated (e.g. massive nosebleed) without necrosis.

arteria colica dextra.c: From the SMA, runs right behind the peritoneum to the ascending colon.
arteria colica dextra.f: Supplies ascending colon; anastomoses with ileocolic and middle colic arteries.
arteria colica dextra.k: Ligated in right hemicolectomy for colon cancer.

arteria colica media.c: From the SMA just below the pancreas, runs in the transverse mesocolon.
arteria colica media.k: Must be protected when opening the transverse mesocolon (e.g. gastric surgery).

arteria colica sinistra.c: First branch of the IMA, runs left retroperitoneally to the descending colon.
arteria colica sinistra.f: Supplies descending colon; joins the marginal artery.
arteria colica sinistra.k: Splenic flexure = watershed between SMA and IMA (Griffiths' point) → ischaemic colitis.

arteria facialis.c: From the external carotid, loops over the submandibular gland, crosses the mandible at the anterior edge of masseter, tortuous to the medial eye angle.
arteria facialis.k: Pulse palpable where it crosses the mandible in front of masseter.

arteria gastrica sinistra.c: Smallest branch of the coeliac trunk, runs up to the cardia then along the lesser curvature.
arteria gastrica sinistra.f: Supplies lesser curvature of the stomach and lower oesophagus.
arteria gastrica sinistra.k: Bleeding posterior gastric ulcer / oesophageal varices (its veins drain to the portal system).

arteria gastroduodenalis.c: From the common hepatic artery, runs behind the first part of the duodenum.
arteria gastroduodenalis.f: Supplies pylorus, duodenum, pancreatic head (gastroepiploic + pancreaticoduodenal arteries).
arteria gastroduodenalis.k: Eroded by a posterior duodenal ulcer → massive upper GI bleeding.

arteria hepatica communis.c: From the coeliac trunk, runs right along the upper pancreas; divides into proper hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries.
arteria hepatica communis.f: Supplies liver, gallbladder, stomach, duodenum, pancreas.
arteria hepatica communis.k: Proper hepatic artery is clamped with the portal vein and CBD in the Pringle manoeuvre.

arteria mesenterica inferior.c: From the aorta at L3, behind the duodenum; branches: left colic, sigmoid, superior rectal.
arteria mesenterica inferior.f: Supplies hindgut: distal third of transverse colon to upper rectum.
arteria mesenterica inferior.k: Often occluded in aortic aneurysm repair – colon survives via the marginal artery.

arteria mesenterica superior.c: From the aorta at L1, passes over the 3rd part of the duodenum into the mesentery.
arteria mesenterica superior.f: Supplies midgut: duodenum (distal), jejunum, ileum, caecum to 2/3 of transverse colon.
arteria mesenterica superior.k: Acute mesenteric ischaemia (embolus) – pain out of proportion to findings; SMA syndrome compresses the duodenum.

arteria occipitalis.c: From the external carotid, runs back under the posterior belly of digastric, pierces trapezius with the greater occipital nerve.
arteria occipitalis.f: Supplies the back of the scalp and neck muscles.
arteria occipitalis.k: Scalp wounds bleed heavily – vessels held open by the dense connective tissue.

arteria rectalis superior.c: Continuation of the IMA, descends in the sigmoid mesocolon to the rectum.
arteria rectalis superior.k: Portosystemic anastomosis with middle/inferior rectal veins in portal hypertension.

arteria splenica.c: Largest coeliac branch, tortuous course along the upper border of the pancreas to the splenic hilum.
arteria splenica.f: Supplies spleen, pancreas body/tail, short gastric and left gastroepiploic arteries.
arteria splenica.k: Splenic artery aneurysm – most common visceral aneurysm, rupture risk in pregnancy.

arteria subclavia.c: Right from the brachiocephalic trunk, left from the arch; arches over the 1st rib behind scalenus anterior.
arteria subclavia.f: Supplies upper limb, brain (vertebral a.), chest wall (internal thoracic a.), thyroid.
arteria subclavia.k: Subclavian steal syndrome: proximal stenosis → arm exercise steals blood from the vertebral artery.

arteria suprascapularis.c: From the thyrocervical trunk, passes OVER the superior transverse scapular ligament (the nerve goes under – 'Army over the bridge, Navy under').
arteria suprascapularis.k: Part of the scapular anastomosis that bypasses an axillary artery block.

arteria temporalis superficialis.c: Terminal branch of the external carotid, ascends in front of the ear over the zygomatic arch.
arteria temporalis superficialis.f: Supplies scalp of the temporal region.
arteria temporalis superficialis.k: Temporal (giant cell) arteritis – tender artery, headache, risk of blindness → biopsy here.

arteriae jejunales.c: 15–18 branches from the left side of the SMA, form arcades in the mesentery.
arteriae jejunales.f: Supply jejunum (few arcades, long vasa recta).
arteriae jejunales.k: Arcade pattern helps the surgeon tell jejunum (long vasa recta) from ileum (many arcades).

arteriae sigmoideae.c: 2–4 branches of the IMA in the sigmoid mesocolon.
arteriae sigmoideae.k: Sigmoid volvulus twists these vessels → ischaemia.

caput longum musculi tricipitis brachii.c: From the infraglenoid tubercle → olecranon; radial nerve.
caput longum musculi tricipitis brachii.f: Extends the elbow, helps adduct/extend the shoulder.
caput longum musculi tricipitis brachii.k: Separates the triangular space (circumflex scapular a.) from the quadrangular space (axillary n.).

centrum tendineum.c: Trefoil-shaped tendon in the middle of the diaphragm, fused with the fibrous pericardium.
centrum tendineum.f: Insertion of all diaphragm muscle fibres; IVC passes through it at T8.
centrum tendineum.k: IVC opening widens in inspiration – helps venous return.

crus dextrum diaphragmatis.c: From the bodies of L1–L3, longer than the left crus; its fibres encircle the oesophageal hiatus (T10).
crus dextrum diaphragmatis.f: Lumbar part of the diaphragm; acts as an external oesophageal sphincter.
crus dextrum diaphragmatis.k: Weakness of the crural sling → sliding hiatal hernia and reflux.

diaphragma.c: From xiphoid, lower 6 ribs and lumbar vertebrae (crura) → central tendon; phrenic nerve C3–C5.
diaphragma.k: 'C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive' – high cervical injury stops breathing; irritation refers pain to the shoulder (C4).

fascia thoracolumbalis.c: Three layers around the deep back muscles, from the sacrum to the neck; attachment of latissimus dorsi and the abdominal muscles.
fascia thoracolumbalis.f: Encloses erector spinae and quadratus lumborum, transmits force between trunk and limbs.
fascia thoracolumbalis.k: Posterior layer is the landmark for lumbar blocks; strain causes low back pain.

fascia transversalis.c: Lines the inner surface of transversus abdominis, between muscle and parietal peritoneum.
fascia transversalis.f: Forms the deep inguinal ring and the posterior wall of the inguinal canal.
fascia transversalis.k: Weakness in Hesselbach's triangle → direct inguinal hernia.

galea aponeurotica.c: Tendon sheet between frontal and occipital bellies of occipitofrontalis – the 'A' of SCALP.
galea aponeurotica.f: Lets the scalp move; frontalis wrinkles the forehead.
galea aponeurotica.k: Gaping scalp wound if the galea is cut; under it lies the 'danger layer' (loose areolar tissue).

glandula submandibularis.c: Wraps around the posterior edge of mylohyoid; duct (Wharton) opens at the sublingual papilla.
glandula submandibularis.f: Produces ~70 % of saliva (mixed); parasympathetic via chorda tympani.
glandula submandibularis.k: Most common site of salivary stones (viscous saliva, duct runs uphill) – swelling while eating.

linea alba.c: Midline fibrous band from xiphoid to pubic symphysis, formed by the interlacing aponeuroses.
linea alba.f: Central anchor of the abdominal wall muscles.
linea alba.k: Avascular midline incision; divarication of the recti and epigastric hernias occur here.

musculi intercostales externi.c: Rib above → rib below, fibres run down and forward ('hands in pockets'); intercostal nerves.
musculi intercostales externi.k: Neurovascular bundle runs in the costal groove under the rib (VAN) → chest drain goes above the lower rib.

musculi intercostales interni.c: Rib below → rib above, fibres at right angles to the external layer; intercostal nerves.
musculi intercostales interni.k: Intercostal nerve block is given at the lower border of the rib.

musculi rhomboidei.c: Spinous processes C7–T5 → medial border of the scapula; dorsal scapular nerve (C5).
musculi rhomboidei.f: Retract and elevate the scapula, rotate the glenoid down.
musculi rhomboidei.k: Dorsal scapular nerve injury → scapula drifts laterally, mild winging.

musculus auricularis anterior.c: From the temporal fascia → front of the auricle; facial nerve.
musculus auricularis anterior.k: One of the muscles of facial expression – all supplied by the facial nerve (VII).

musculus auricularis posterior.c: From the mastoid → back of the auricle; posterior auricular branch of the facial nerve.
musculus auricularis posterior.k: Its nerve leaves VII just after the stylomastoid foramen – spared only in very distal lesions.

musculus auricularis superior.c: From the galea aponeurotica → upper auricle; facial nerve.
musculus auricularis superior.k: Largest of the auricular muscles; vestigial in humans.

musculus buccinator.c: From pterygomandibular raphe and alveolar processes → angle of the mouth; facial nerve; pierced by the parotid duct.
musculus buccinator.f: Presses the cheek against the teeth – keeps food between the molars, blowing.
musculus buccinator.k: Facial palsy → food collects in the cheek vestibule.

musculus constrictor pharyngis inferior.c: From thyroid and cricoid cartilage → pharyngeal raphe; vagus (pharyngeal plexus).
musculus constrictor pharyngis inferior.f: Squeezes the bolus down; its cricopharyngeal part is the upper oesophageal sphincter.
musculus constrictor pharyngis inferior.k: Killian's dehiscence between its two parts → Zenker's diverticulum.

musculus constrictor pharyngis medius.c: From the hyoid bone and stylohyoid ligament → pharyngeal raphe; vagus.
musculus constrictor pharyngis medius.k: Glossopharyngeal nerve and stylopharyngeus pass between middle and superior constrictor.

musculus constrictor pharyngis superior.c: From pterygomandibular raphe and medial pterygoid plate → pharyngeal raphe; vagus.
musculus constrictor pharyngis superior.f: Constricts the upper pharynx, seals the nasopharynx in swallowing.
musculus constrictor pharyngis superior.k: Lies just behind the palatine tonsil – peritonsillar abscess spreads along it.

musculus coracobrachialis.c: From the coracoid process → middle of the humerus; pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.
musculus coracobrachialis.k: Landmark: the musculocutaneous nerve enters it about 5 cm below the coracoid.

musculus corrugator supercilii.c: From the medial supraorbital margin → skin of the eyebrow; facial nerve.
musculus corrugator supercilii.k: Target of botulinum toxin for vertical frown lines.

musculus deltoideus.c: From clavicle, acromion and spine of scapula → deltoid tuberosity; axillary nerve (C5–C6).
musculus deltoideus.f: Abducts the arm (15–90°), anterior part flexes, posterior part extends.
musculus deltoideus.k: Surgical neck fracture / shoulder dislocation → axillary nerve palsy: flat shoulder, numb 'regimental badge' area.

musculus depressor anguli oris.c: From the oblique line of the mandible → angle of the mouth; facial nerve.
musculus depressor anguli oris.f: Pulls the corner of the mouth down – sad face.
musculus depressor anguli oris.k: Its weakness gives the asymmetric 'crying face' in newborns with facial nerve lesions.

musculus depressor labii inferioris.c: From the mandible below the depressor anguli → lower lip; marginal mandibular branch of VII.
musculus depressor labii inferioris.k: Marginal mandibular nerve injury in submandibular surgery → asymmetric smile.

musculus erector spinae.c: Common origin from sacrum, iliac crest and lumbar spines; three columns – lateral to medial 'I Love Spine': iliocostalis, longissimus, spinalis; dorsal rami.
musculus erector spinae.f: Extends and laterally bends the vertebral column, keeps posture.
musculus erector spinae.k: Spasm of erector spinae is a common cause of acute low back pain.

musculus hyoglossus.c: From the greater horn of the hyoid → side of the tongue; hypoglossal nerve.
musculus hyoglossus.k: Key landmark: lingual nerve and XII run on it, lingual artery runs deep to it.

musculus iliacus.c: From the iliac fossa → lesser trochanter (with psoas = iliopsoas); femoral nerve.
musculus iliacus.k: Iliacus haematoma (anticoagulation) compresses the femoral nerve.

musculus iliocostalis.c: Lateral column of erector spinae: iliac crest / sacrum → angles of the ribs and cervical transverse processes; dorsal rami.
musculus iliocostalis.f: Extends and laterally flexes the trunk.
musculus iliocostalis.k: 'I Love Spine': Iliocostalis is the most lateral column.

musculus iliocostalis cervicis.c: From the angles of ribs 3–6 → transverse processes C4–C6; dorsal rami.
musculus iliocostalis cervicis.f: Extends and laterally bends the neck.
musculus iliocostalis cervicis.k: Upper end of the lateral column of erector spinae.

musculus infraspinatus.c: From the infraspinous fossa → middle facet of the greater tubercle; suprascapular nerve (C5–C6).
musculus infraspinatus.f: Lateral rotation of the arm; rotator cuff stabiliser.
musculus infraspinatus.k: Suprascapular nerve entrapment at the spinoglenoid notch → isolated infraspinatus wasting (volleyball players).

musculus latissimus dorsi.c: From spines T7–L5, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lower ribs → floor of the intertubercular groove; thoracodorsal nerve (C6–C8).
musculus latissimus dorsi.f: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the arm – climbing, swimming.
musculus latissimus dorsi.k: Used as a pedicled flap for breast reconstruction; thoracodorsal nerve at risk in axillary clearance.

musculus levator anguli oris.c: From the canine fossa of the maxilla → angle of the mouth; facial nerve.
musculus levator anguli oris.f: Lifts the corner of the mouth.
musculus levator anguli oris.k: Infraorbital nerve emerges between it and levator labii superioris – block site.

musculus levator labii superioris.c: From the infraorbital margin → upper lip; facial nerve.

musculus levator labii superioris alaequ.c: From the frontal process of the maxilla → ala of the nose and upper lip; facial nerve.
musculus levator labii superioris alaequ.f: Raises the lip and flares the nostril ('Elvis sneer').
musculus levator labii superioris alaequ.k: Longest muscle name in the body – a favourite clip-test question.

musculus levator scapulae.c: From transverse processes C1–C4 → superior angle of the scapula; dorsal scapular nerve + C3–C4.
musculus levator scapulae.f: Elevates the scapula and rotates the glenoid down; bends the neck.
musculus levator scapulae.k: Common site of 'stiff neck' – trigger point at the superior angle.

musculus longissimus.c: Middle column of erector spinae: from the common tendon → transverse processes and ribs, up to the mastoid; dorsal rami.
musculus longissimus.f: Extends and laterally bends the spine and head.
musculus longissimus.k: Longest and thickest column – 'I Love Spine'.

musculus longissimus capitis.c: From transverse processes T1–T5 / articular processes C4–C7 → mastoid process; dorsal rami.
musculus longissimus capitis.f: Extends the head, turns it to the same side.
musculus longissimus capitis.k: Only part of erector spinae that reaches the skull.

musculus masseter.c: From the zygomatic arch → lateral ramus and angle of mandible; masseteric nerve (V3).
musculus masseter.k: Palpable when clenching; tested for V3 function; hypertrophy in bruxism.

musculus mentalis.c: From the incisive fossa of the mandible → skin of the chin; facial nerve.
musculus mentalis.f: Raises and wrinkles the chin, protrudes the lower lip (pouting).
musculus mentalis.k: Only muscle that elevates the lower lip.

musculus mylohyoideus.c: From the mylohyoid line of the mandible → hyoid and midline raphe; nerve to mylohyoid (V3).
musculus mylohyoideus.f: Forms the floor of the mouth; raises the hyoid and tongue in swallowing.
musculus mylohyoideus.k: Ludwig's angina spreads above and below it; submandibular gland curls around its free border.

musculus nasalis.c: From the maxilla above the canine → nasal cartilages; facial nerve.
musculus nasalis.f: Compresses (transverse part) or flares (alar part) the nostrils.
musculus nasalis.k: Nasal flaring = sign of respiratory distress in children.

musculus obliquus externus abdominis.c: From the outer surface of ribs 5–12 → linea alba, pubic tubercle, iliac crest; fibres 'hands in pockets'; T7–T12 + L1.
musculus obliquus externus abdominis.f: Flexes and rotates the trunk (to the opposite side), raises abdominal pressure.
musculus obliquus externus abdominis.k: Its aponeurosis forms the inguinal ligament and the superficial inguinal ring.

musculus obliquus internus abdominis.c: From thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lateral inguinal ligament → lower ribs, linea alba; T7–L1.
musculus obliquus internus abdominis.f: Flexes and rotates the trunk (same side), abdominal pressure.
musculus obliquus internus abdominis.k: Forms the conjoint tendon and the cremaster muscle.

musculus orbicularis oculi.c: Ring around the orbit: orbital, palpebral and lacrimal parts; temporal and zygomatic branches of VII.
musculus orbicularis oculi.f: Closes the eyelids – blinking (palpebral) and squeezing (orbital).
musculus orbicularis oculi.k: Facial palsy → eye cannot close → corneal drying (exposure keratitis).

musculus orbicularis oris.c: Sphincter of the lips, many fibres from the other mouth muscles; buccal and marginal mandibular branches of VII.
musculus orbicularis oris.f: Closes and purses the lips – whistling, kissing, speech.
musculus orbicularis oris.k: Facial palsy → drooling and dribbling from the affected corner.

musculus pectoralis major.c: Clavicular head (clavicle) and sternocostal head (sternum, ribs 1–6) → lateral lip of intertubercular groove; medial and lateral pectoral nerves.
musculus pectoralis major.f: Adducts and medially rotates the arm; clavicular head flexes.
musculus pectoralis major.k: Poland syndrome = congenital absence of the sternocostal head; used as a reconstructive flap.

musculus pectoralis minor.c: From ribs 3–5 → coracoid process; medial pectoral nerve.
musculus pectoralis minor.f: Depresses and protracts the scapula; accessory inspiratory muscle.
musculus pectoralis minor.k: Landmark dividing the axillary artery into 3 parts and the axillary lymph nodes into levels I–III.

musculus procerus.c: From the nasal bone → skin between the eyebrows; facial nerve.
musculus procerus.f: Pulls the medial eyebrow down – horizontal wrinkles at the nose root.
musculus procerus.k: Treated with botulinum toxin together with corrugator.

musculus psoas major.c: From T12–L5 vertebral bodies and transverse processes → lesser trochanter; ventral rami L1–L3; lumbar plexus lies inside it.
musculus psoas major.f: Flexes the hip (iliopsoas), flexes the trunk.
musculus psoas major.k: Psoas sign in retrocaecal appendicitis; psoas abscess (TB spine) tracks down to the groin.

musculus psoas minor.c: From T12–L1 → iliopubic eminence; L1. Absent in about 40 %.
musculus psoas minor.k: Its frequent absence makes it a favourite 'is it there?' clip question.

musculus pterygoideus lateralis.c: Two heads from the greater wing of sphenoid / lateral pterygoid plate → neck of mandible and TMJ disc; V3.
musculus pterygoideus lateralis.f: Opens the mouth and protrudes the jaw; side-to-side grinding.
musculus pterygoideus lateralis.k: Only muscle that opens the jaw; involved in TMJ disc displacement.

musculus pyramidalis.c: From the pubic body → linea alba, in front of rectus abdominis inside the rectus sheath; subcostal nerve (T12).
musculus pyramidalis.k: Absent in ~20 %; landmark for midline in lower incisions.

musculus quadratus lumborum.c: From the iliac crest → 12th rib and L1–L4 transverse processes; T12–L4.
musculus quadratus lumborum.f: Lateral flexion of the trunk, fixes the 12th rib in inspiration.
musculus quadratus lumborum.k: Quadratus lumborum block for abdominal surgery pain; common source of low back pain.

musculus rectus abdominis.c: From the pubic crest/symphysis → xiphoid and costal cartilages 5–7; tendinous intersections ('six-pack'); T7–T12.
musculus rectus abdominis.f: Flexes the trunk, raises abdominal pressure.
musculus rectus abdominis.k: Rectus sheath haematoma (inferior epigastric artery) – painful mass, mimics acute abdomen.

musculus rhomboideus major.c: From spinous processes T2–T5 → medial border of scapula below the spine; dorsal scapular nerve (C5).
musculus rhomboideus major.k: Lies deep to trapezius – a classic clip-test structure of the superficial back.

musculus risorius.c: From the parotid/masseteric fascia → angle of the mouth; facial nerve.
musculus risorius.f: Pulls the corner of the mouth laterally – 'grin'.
musculus risorius.k: Spasm gives the risus sardonicus of tetanus.

musculus scalenus anterior.c: From transverse processes C3–C6 → scalene tubercle of the 1st rib; ventral rami C4–C6.
musculus scalenus anterior.f: Elevates the 1st rib, flexes the neck.
musculus scalenus anterior.k: Phrenic nerve runs on it; subclavian vein in front, artery + brachial plexus behind it (scalene gap) → thoracic outlet syndrome.

musculus scalenus medius.c: From transverse processes C2–C7 → 1st rib behind the subclavian groove; cervical ventral rami.
musculus scalenus medius.f: Elevates the 1st rib, bends the neck.
musculus scalenus medius.k: Brachial plexus and subclavian artery pass between scalenus anterior and medius – interscalene block.

musculus semispinalis capitis.c: From transverse processes C4–T6 → between the nuchal lines of the occiput; dorsal rami; pierced by the greater occipital nerve.
musculus semispinalis capitis.k: Greater occipital nerve can be compressed where it pierces it → occipital neuralgia.

musculus serratus anterior.c: From ribs 1–8/9 (saw-tooth slips) → costal surface of the medial border of the scapula; long thoracic nerve (C5–C7).
musculus serratus anterior.f: Protracts the scapula (boxer's punch), rotates it up for abduction > 90°.
musculus serratus anterior.k: Long thoracic nerve injury (axillary surgery) → winged scapula when pushing against a wall.

musculus serratus posterior inferior.c: From spinous processes T11–L2 → ribs 9–12; intercostal nerves T9–T12.
musculus serratus posterior inferior.k: Thin muscle of the intermediate back layer, lies on erector spinae.

musculus serratus posterior superior.c: From spinous processes C7–T3 → ribs 2–5; intercostal nerves T2–T5.
musculus serratus posterior superior.k: Intermediate back layer, under the rhomboids.

musculus spinalis.c: Medial column of erector spinae: spinous processes → spinous processes; dorsal rami.
musculus spinalis.k: 'I Love Spine': spinalis is the most medial column, next to the spinous processes.

musculus splenius capitis.c: From the ligamentum nuchae and spines C7–T4 → mastoid and superior nuchal line; dorsal rami C2–C3.
musculus splenius capitis.f: Extends the head and turns it to the same side.
musculus splenius capitis.k: Bandage-like 'splenius' wraps the deep neck muscles – injured in whiplash.

musculus splenius cervicis.c: From spines T3–T6 → transverse processes C1–C3; dorsal rami.
musculus splenius cervicis.f: Extends and rotates the neck to the same side.
musculus splenius cervicis.k: Lower part of the splenius sheet, lies under trapezius and rhomboids.

musculus sternocleidomastoideus.c: From manubrium and medial clavicle → mastoid process; accessory nerve (XI) + C2–C3.
musculus sternocleidomastoideus.f: One side: tilts head to same side, turns face to opposite side; both: flex neck.
musculus sternocleidomastoideus.k: Congenital torticollis (fibrosis in newborns); divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.

musculus sternohyoideus.c: From the manubrium → body of the hyoid; ansa cervicalis.

musculus sternothyroideus.c: From the manubrium (under sternohyoid) → oblique line of thyroid cartilage; ansa cervicalis.
musculus sternothyroideus.k: Lies directly on the thyroid gland – first muscle met in thyroid surgery.

musculus stylohyoideus.c: From the styloid process → hyoid (split around the digastric tendon); facial nerve.
musculus stylohyoideus.f: Elevates and retracts the hyoid in swallowing.
musculus stylohyoideus.k: Eagle syndrome: long styloid / calcified ligament causes throat pain.

musculus subscapularis.c: From the subscapular fossa → lesser tubercle; upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5–C6).
musculus subscapularis.f: Medial rotation of the arm; rotator cuff ('SITS').
musculus subscapularis.k: Lift-off test (Gerber) checks it; prevents anterior shoulder dislocation.

musculus supraspinatus.c: From the supraspinous fossa → upper facet of greater tubercle, under the acromion; suprascapular nerve (C5).
musculus supraspinatus.k: Most commonly torn cuff tendon – painful arc 60–120° (impingement).

musculus temporalis.c: From the temporal fossa → coronoid process; deep temporal nerves (V3).
musculus temporalis.k: Felt contracting at the temple when clenching; tension headache source.

musculus teres major.c: From the inferior angle of the scapula → medial lip of intertubercular groove; lower subscapular nerve.
musculus teres major.f: Adducts and medially rotates the arm ('lat's little helper').
musculus teres major.k: Lower border of teres major = where the axillary artery becomes brachial.

musculus teres minor.c: From the lateral border of scapula → lower facet of greater tubercle; axillary nerve.
musculus teres minor.k: Forms the upper border of the quadrangular space (axillary nerve + posterior circumflex humeral a.).

musculus thyrohyoideus.c: From the oblique line of thyroid cartilage → hyoid; C1 fibres via the hypoglossal nerve.
musculus thyrohyoideus.f: Depresses the hyoid / raises the larynx.
musculus thyrohyoideus.k: Only infrahyoid muscle NOT supplied by the ansa cervicalis.

musculus transversus abdominis.c: From the inner costal cartilages 7–12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest → linea alba; T7–L1. Fibres run horizontally.
musculus transversus abdominis.f: Compresses the abdomen – 'natural corset', core stability.
musculus transversus abdominis.k: TAP block: local anaesthetic between internal oblique and transversus.

musculus trapezius.c: From the occiput, ligamentum nuchae, spines C7–T12 → lateral clavicle, acromion, spine of scapula; accessory nerve (XI).
musculus trapezius.f: Upper part elevates (shrug), middle retracts, lower depresses the scapula; rotates it up.
musculus trapezius.k: XI injury in posterior triangle surgery → shoulder droops, cannot shrug.

musculus zygomaticus major.c: From the zygomatic bone → angle of the mouth; zygomatic and buccal branches of VII.
musculus zygomaticus major.f: Pulls the corner of the mouth up and out – smiling.
musculus zygomaticus major.k: Its action is lost on the paralysed side in Bell's palsy – flat smile.

nervi supraclaviculares.c: From C3–C4, emerge at Erb's point, fan down over the clavicle (medial, intermediate, lateral).
nervi supraclaviculares.f: Sensory to skin over clavicle, shoulder and upper chest.
nervi supraclaviculares.k: Shoulder-tip pain from diaphragm irritation is referred through C4 (same root).

nervus accessorius.c: CN XI: leaves the skull through the jugular foramen, pierces SCM, crosses the posterior triangle superficially to trapezius.
nervus accessorius.k: Easily cut in lymph-node biopsy of the posterior triangle → cannot shrug, shoulder droops.

nervus alveolaris inferior.c: Branch of V3, enters the mandibular foramen, runs in the mandibular canal, exits as the mental nerve; gives the nerve to mylohyoid.
nervus alveolaris inferior.f: Sensory to the lower teeth; motor to mylohyoid and anterior digastric.
nervus alveolaris inferior.k: Inferior alveolar block numbs the lower teeth and half the lip; injured in wisdom-tooth extraction.

nervus auricularis magnus.c: From C2–C3, winds around the posterior border of SCM at Erb's point and runs up to the ear.
nervus auricularis magnus.f: Sensory to the skin over the parotid, angle of the jaw and auricle.
nervus auricularis magnus.k: Often injured in parotid surgery → numb earlobe; used as a nerve graft.

nervus auriculotemporalis.c: Branch of V3, encircles the middle meningeal artery, runs behind the TMJ and up with the superficial temporal artery.
nervus auriculotemporalis.f: Sensory to temple and ear; carries parasympathetic fibres (IX) to the parotid.
nervus auriculotemporalis.k: Frey's syndrome after parotidectomy – sweating of the cheek while eating.

nervus axillaris.c: From the posterior cord (C5–C6), passes through the quadrangular space around the surgical neck of the humerus.
nervus axillaris.f: Motor to deltoid and teres minor; skin over the lower deltoid.
nervus axillaris.k: Surgical neck fracture / shoulder dislocation → loss of abduction, numb 'regimental badge' patch.

nervus hypoglossus.c: CN XII: hypoglossal canal → between ICA and IJV, loops forward over the external carotid onto hyoglossus.
nervus hypoglossus.f: Motor to all tongue muscles except palatoglossus.
nervus hypoglossus.k: Lesion → tongue deviates to the SAME side on protrusion ('lick your wounds').

nervus iliohypogastricus.c: From L1, emerges at the lateral border of psoas, crosses quadratus lumborum, pierces transversus abdominis.
nervus iliohypogastricus.f: Motor to lower abdominal muscles; sensory to suprapubic and lateral gluteal skin.
nervus iliohypogastricus.k: Can be injured in appendectomy / Pfannenstiel incisions → numbness and bulging.

nervus infraorbitalis.c: Continuation of V2, runs in the orbital floor and exits at the infraorbital foramen.
nervus infraorbitalis.f: Sensory to lower eyelid, cheek, side of the nose and upper lip.
nervus infraorbitalis.k: Orbital floor (blow-out) fracture → numb cheek and upper lip.

nervus intercostalis.c: Ventral rami T1–T11, run in the costal groove under each rib, in the VAN bundle between internal and innermost intercostals.
nervus intercostalis.f: Motor to intercostal muscles, sensory to chest and abdominal skin (dermatomes).
nervus intercostalis.k: Herpes zoster follows one intercostal dermatome; chest drains go over the upper border of the rib below.

nervus laryngeus recurrens.c: From the vagus; right hooks around the subclavian artery, left around the aortic arch; ascends in the tracheo-oesophageal groove.
nervus laryngeus recurrens.f: Motor to all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid; sensory below the vocal folds.
nervus laryngeus recurrens.k: Injured in thyroidectomy or by lung/aortic tumours → hoarseness; bilateral → stridor.

nervus lingualis.c: Branch of V3, joined by chorda tympani, runs under the 3rd molar, loops under the submandibular duct.
nervus lingualis.f: General sensation (and taste via VII) of the anterior 2/3 of the tongue; parasympathetic to submandibular/sublingual glands.
nervus lingualis.k: Damaged in wisdom-tooth extraction → numb tongue and loss of taste.

nervus mentalis.c: Terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve, exits the mental foramen below the 2nd premolar.
nervus mentalis.f: Sensory to chin and lower lip.
nervus mentalis.k: Numb chin syndrome can be the first sign of metastatic cancer in the mandible.

nervus occipitalis major.c: Dorsal ramus of C2, curls around obliquus capitis inferior, pierces semispinalis capitis and trapezius, rises with the occipital artery.
nervus occipitalis major.f: Sensory to the back of the scalp up to the vertex.
nervus occipitalis major.k: Occipital neuralgia – shooting pain over the back of the head; nerve block relieves it.

nervus occipitalis minor.c: From C2 (cervical plexus), emerges at Erb's point, runs up along the posterior border of SCM.
nervus occipitalis minor.f: Sensory to skin behind the ear.
nervus occipitalis minor.k: One of the 4 cutaneous nerves at Erb's point – a classic clip-test structure.

nervus splanchnicus major.c: Preganglionic sympathetic fibres from T5–T9 ganglia, run down on the vertebral bodies, pierce the crus to the coeliac ganglion.
nervus splanchnicus major.f: Sympathetic supply to foregut organs (via the coeliac plexus).
nervus splanchnicus major.k: Carries visceral pain from the upper abdomen – coeliac plexus block for pancreatic cancer pain.

nervus subcostalis.c: Ventral ramus of T12, runs below the 12th rib, in front of quadratus lumborum, behind the kidney.
nervus subcostalis.f: Motor to lower abdominal wall; sensory to skin above the iliac crest and groin.
nervus subcostalis.k: Injured in flank incisions for kidney surgery → bulging of the abdominal wall.

nervus suprascapularis.c: From the upper trunk (C5–C6), passes UNDER the superior transverse scapular ligament through the suprascapular notch.
nervus suprascapularis.f: Motor to supraspinatus and infraspinatus; sensory to the shoulder joint.
nervus suprascapularis.k: Entrapment at the notch → weak abduction and lateral rotation with wasting above and below the spine.

nervus vagus.c: CN X: jugular foramen → in the carotid sheath between IJV and carotid → mediastinum (right behind the bronchus, left over the arch) → oesophageal plexus → abdomen.
nervus vagus.f: Parasympathetic to heart, lungs and gut to the splenic flexure; motor to pharynx and larynx.
nervus vagus.k: Lesion → uvula deviates to the healthy side, hoarseness; vagal stimulation slows the heart (carotid massage).

oesophagus.c: From C6 (cricoid) to T11, behind the trachea and left atrium, through the diaphragm at T10.
oesophagus.f: Transports food by peristalsis; upper and lower sphincters.
oesophagus.k: Narrowings (cricoid, aortic arch, left bronchus, diaphragm) are where foreign bodies lodge and cancers occur.

platysma.c: Thin sheet in the superficial fascia from the upper chest → mandible and lower face; cervical branch of VII.
platysma.f: Tenses the neck skin, pulls the mouth corner down.
platysma.k: Must be sutured separately in neck incisions for a good scar; 'turkey neck' with age.

plexus brachialis.c: Ventral rami C5–T1: Roots → Trunks → Divisions → Cords → Branches ('Read That Damn Cadaver Book'); roots/trunks between the scalenes, cords around the axillary artery.
plexus brachialis.f: Motor and sensory supply of the whole upper limb.
plexus brachialis.k: Erb's palsy (C5–C6, 'waiter's tip'); Klumpke's palsy (C8–T1, claw hand).

plexus cervicalis.c: Ventral rami C1–C4, deep to SCM; cutaneous branches emerge at Erb's point (punctum nervosum) at the middle of the posterior border of SCM.
plexus cervicalis.f: Skin of neck and scalp (lesser occipital, great auricular, transverse cervical, supraclavicular), ansa cervicalis, phrenic nerve.
plexus cervicalis.k: Superficial cervical plexus block at Erb's point for carotid surgery.

plexus coeliacus.c: Around the coeliac trunk at T12–L1; receives greater and lesser splanchnic nerves and vagal fibres.
plexus coeliacus.f: Autonomic supply to stomach, liver, pancreas, spleen, small intestine.
plexus coeliacus.k: Coeliac plexus block (alcohol) relieves pain of pancreatic cancer.

truncus coeliacus.c: From the aorta at T12 just below the median arcuate ligament; trifurcates: left gastric, splenic, common hepatic.
truncus coeliacus.f: Supplies the foregut: stomach, liver, spleen, pancreas, duodenum (part).
truncus coeliacus.k: Median arcuate ligament syndrome: compression of the trunk → post-meal pain and weight loss.

truncus sympathicus.c: Chain of ganglia from the skull base to the coccyx, along the vertebral bodies / rib heads.
truncus sympathicus.f: Distributes sympathetic fibres to the body wall and organs.
truncus sympathicus.k: Lesion of the cervical part → Horner's syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis); Pancoast tumour.

vagina musculi recti abdominis.c: Aponeuroses of the 3 flat muscles enclose rectus abdominis; below the arcuate line all layers pass in front of it.
vagina musculi recti abdominis.f: Holds rectus in place, contains the epigastric vessels.
vagina musculi recti abdominis.k: Below the arcuate line only the transversalis fascia lies behind rectus – weak spot; rectus sheath block for midline surgery.

vena brachiocephalica.c: Formed behind the sternoclavicular joint by IJV + subclavian vein; the left one crosses the midline above the arch; both form the SVC.
vena brachiocephalica.f: Drains head, neck and upper limbs.
vena brachiocephalica.k: Left vein is long and crosses the midline – at risk in sternotomy and compressed by thymomas.

vena cava superior.c: Formed behind the right 1st costal cartilage by both brachiocephalic veins; receives the azygos vein; enters the right atrium.
vena cava superior.f: Drains everything above the diaphragm (except heart and lungs).
vena cava superior.k: SVC syndrome (lung cancer) → swollen face and arms, distended neck veins.

vena facialis.c: Starts at the medial eye angle (angular vein), runs down behind the facial artery, joins the retromandibular vein → IJV.
vena facialis.k: Danger triangle: connects via ophthalmic veins with the cavernous sinus → infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis.

vena jugularis externa.c: Formed behind the angle of the mandible (posterior auricular + retromandibular), crosses SCM obliquely, ends in the subclavian vein.
vena jugularis externa.k: Visible when raised venous pressure (heart failure); used for venous access.

vena jugularis interna.c: From the jugular foramen (sigmoid sinus), runs in the carotid sheath lateral to the carotid, joins the subclavian vein behind the sternoclavicular joint.
vena jugularis interna.f: Main venous drainage of brain, face and neck.
vena jugularis interna.k: JVP measured on the right IJV; central venous catheters go in between the two heads of SCM.

vena mesenterica inferior.c: Ascends left of the duodenojejunal flexure, behind the pancreas into the splenic vein.
vena mesenterica inferior.f: Drains the hindgut (left colon, rectum) to the portal system.
vena mesenterica inferior.k: Its rectal tributaries form portosystemic anastomoses in portal hypertension.

vena mesenterica superior.c: Right of the SMA in the mesentery, crosses the 3rd part of the duodenum, joins the splenic vein behind the pancreatic neck = portal vein.
vena mesenterica superior.k: Invasion by pancreatic head cancer decides if the tumour is resectable.

vena portae hepatis.c: Formed behind the pancreatic neck (SMV + splenic vein), runs up in the free edge of the lesser omentum behind the bile duct and hepatic artery.
vena portae hepatis.f: Brings nutrient-rich blood from gut and spleen to the liver (~75 % of liver blood).
vena portae hepatis.k: Portal hypertension (cirrhosis) → oesophageal varices, caput medusae, haemorrhoids, splenomegaly.

vena retromandibularis.c: Formed in the parotid by superficial temporal + maxillary veins, divides into anterior (→ facial) and posterior (→ external jugular) branches.
vena retromandibularis.f: Drains the temple and deep face.
vena retromandibularis.k: Landmark in parotidectomy – the facial nerve lies just superficial to it.

vena splenica.c: From the splenic hilum along the back of the pancreas, joins the SMV to form the portal vein.
vena splenica.f: Drains spleen, pancreas and stomach (short gastric veins).
vena splenica.k: Splenic vein thrombosis (pancreatitis) → isolated gastric varices.

vena subclavia.c: Continues the axillary vein at the 1st rib, runs in FRONT of scalenus anterior, joins the IJV (venous angle) – thoracic duct opens on the left.
vena subclavia.k: Subclavian central line insertion – risk of pneumothorax.

vena thyroidea inferior.c: From the lower thyroid pole, descends in front of the trachea into the brachiocephalic veins.
vena thyroidea inferior.k: Must be ligated in tracheostomy and thyroid surgery – bleeds easily.

venter anterior musculi digastrici.c: From the digastric fossa of the mandible → intermediate tendon on the hyoid; nerve to mylohyoid (V3).
venter anterior musculi digastrici.f: Depresses the mandible, raises the hyoid.
venter anterior musculi digastrici.k: Different nerves for the two bellies show their different embryological arches (1st vs 2nd).

venter frontalis musculi occipitofrontal.c: From the galea aponeurotica → skin of the eyebrows; temporal branch of VII.
venter frontalis musculi occipitofrontal.f: Raises the eyebrows, wrinkles the forehead.
venter frontalis musculi occipitofrontal.k: Central (UMN) facial palsy spares the forehead – peripheral (Bell's) palsy does not.

venter inferior musculi omohyoidei.c: From the upper border of the scapula → intermediate tendon (held to the clavicle by fascia); ansa cervicalis.
venter inferior musculi omohyoidei.k: Divides the posterior triangle into occipital and supraclavicular triangles.

venter occipitalis musculi occipitofront.c: From the superior nuchal line → galea aponeurotica; posterior auricular branch of VII.
venter occipitalis musculi occipitofront.k: Together with the frontal belly and the galea it forms the 'A' of SCALP.

venter posterior musculi digastrici.c: From the mastoid notch → intermediate tendon on the hyoid; facial nerve.
venter posterior musculi digastrici.f: Raises the hyoid, helps open the mouth.
venter posterior musculi digastrici.k: Key landmark of the upper neck: IJV, ICA, XI and XII run deep to it.

venter superior musculi omohyoidei.c: From the intermediate tendon → body of the hyoid; ansa cervicalis.
venter superior musculi omohyoidei.k: Crosses the carotid sheath at the level of the cricoid – landmark in neck dissection.
